# SB-1033 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

## Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during shot blasting operations in the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) presents inhalation, combustible dust, and visibility hazards for operators and maintenance personnel. The blast process liberates fines from scale, oxides, and shot degradation that can remain suspended in the cabinet plume during and after blasting. Migration of fines outside the cabinet during door cycles or while performing inspection and maintenance increases the risk of respiratory exposure and secondary contamination of adjacent work areas on P3, line P3-L1. Accumulation of this dust in housings, on motor enclosures, and in ventilation plenums can contribute to equipment wear and degrade dust control effectiveness.

Background: Recent inspections and a review of maintenance records identified recurring dust ingress through the access seals and liner interfaces of EQ-P3-L1-SB02. Loose or incorrectly torqued liner fasteners allow liner movement, increasing abrasive wear and particulate generation. Proper mechanical retention of the blast wheel liner and consistent housekeeping and controls reduce airborne release and downstream exposure.

Rationale: Controlling the source by maintaining liner integrity reduces the rate of particulate generation, which in turn improves capture efficiency of local extraction and simplifies post-operation cleanup. Consistent torque on liner bolts prevents fretting and migration that lead to increased wear and dust release during operation and maintenance.

Related documents: MM-P3-L1-SB02, SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-03

## Affected equipment
- Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) located on P3, line P3-L1.  
- Associated capture and extraction ductwork serving EQ-P3-L1-SB02.  
- Routine maintenance tools and fixtures used for liner replacement and inspection on EQ-P3-L1-SB02.

Note: Personnel who open the cabinet, perform inspection, replace liners, or work near extraction doors are considered affected. Maintenance activities performed in accordance with MM-P3-L1-SB02 and procedures SOP-P3-L1-02 or SOP-P3-L1-03 must incorporate the controls below.

## Required controls
Administrative and engineering controls described below are mandatory for operations and maintenance of EQ-P3-L1-SB02.

1. Mechanical retention
   - The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 65 N·m. Verify and record torque after any liner work and during scheduled inspections defined in MM-P3-L1-SB02. Use a calibrated torque wrench traceable per MM-P3-L1-SB02 for this verification.

2. Procedure adherence
   - Perform liner replacement, inspection, and bolt torque verification in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03. Before any door opening, ensure the cabinet is isolated and the extraction system is operating per those procedures to minimize dust migration.

3. Local extraction and containment
   - Ensure the cabinet’s capture system is operational during blasting and for an appropriate stabilization period prior to door opening as specified in SOP-P3-L1-02. When extraction is unavailable, do not operate EQ-P3-L1-SB02.

4. Housekeeping and cleaning
   - After liner work or visible dust release, perform wet or HEPA-filtered vacuum cleanup of accessible surfaces to prevent re-entrainment. Do not dry sweep residues that may become airborne.

5. Personal protective equipment (PPE)
   - Use respiratory protection and other PPE required by SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03 when entering the cabinet envelope or performing cleanup where dust is present. Selection of respiratory protection shall follow the hazard assessment in those procedures.

6. Training and authorization
   - Only personnel trained and authorized per MM-P3-L1-SB02 and SOP-P3-L1-03 may perform liner replacement or bolt torque verification on EQ-P3-L1-SB02.

7. Verification and corrective action
   - If any bolt is found outside the specified torque, stop the operation, document the condition, retorque to 65 N·m, and inspect liners and adjacent components for accelerated wear before returning the cabinet to service.

Examples:
- Example 1: During a scheduled inspection, a technician finds multiple liner bolts loose. The technician isolates EQ-P3-L1-SB02, starts extraction, removes residual dust using HEPA vacuum, and retorques each bolt to 65 N·m. The technician records the action in the maintenance log and notifies the supervisor for a follow-up inspection under MM-P3-L1-SB02.
- Example 2: After an unplanned liner change, the responsible technician verifies torque on all fasteners, documents torque readings per SOP-P3-L1-03, and confirms extraction performance before the next production run.

Records to keep:
- Maintenance log entries for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 that record liner removal, installation, and verification steps, with explicit statement that the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) was set to 65 N·m. Retain entries as described by MM-P3-L1-SB02.
- Calibration certificate for torque wrench used, filed per MM-P3-L1-SB02.
- Procedure compliance checklists completed per SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03 for each maintenance event.
- Incident reports for any evidence of dust escape or unplanned exposures, with corrective actions documented.

Audit and inspection:
- Supervisors shall review maintenance logs and PPE compliance for activities involving EQ-P3-L1-SB02. Findings requiring rework or retraining should reference SOP-P3-L1-02 for operation controls and SOP-P3-L1-03 for maintenance steps. Ensure corrective actions are entered into the site control system per MM-P3-L1-SB02.

## Effective date
Effective: Rev E

Distribution: All maintenance personnel, shift leads, and safety representatives responsible for P3, line P3-L1 and EQ-P3-L1-SB02 must review this bulletin and the referenced documents MM-P3-L1-SB02, SOP-P3-L1-02, and SOP-P3-L1-03 before performing related activities.
